Subject: RFI -- SLA measurement validation checklist for EU private deploy

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As part of our security and procurement approval we need a concise checklist that explains exactly how Redwood will measure uptime and latency for our EU private deployment (VPC-connected, on-prem probes for ingestion). Procurement wants this to include:

- authoritative measurement sources (Redwood internal telemetry, Novus client-side telemetry, third-party probes)
- sampling cadence and aggregation windows for latency percentiles
- clock sync assumptions and allowable drift between probes
- regional attribution rules when traffic is split across AZs/regions
- synthetic probe placement and acceptance test procedures
- the formula and timing for calculating service credits (if any) and the evidence required to claim them

I've attached Novus's standard RFI PDF with the section highlighted. Can you confirm you can produce a single checklist doc with acceptance criteria that our auditors can sign off on? We are aiming to finalize procurement terms by Aug 8.

Attachments: novus_sla_rfi.pdf

Marta,

Thanks — we can do that. High level summary below; we'll compile the checklist and acceptance criteria into a single PDF and share before Aug 4. Key points summarized here so your audit team has immediate visibility: 

1) Authoritative measurement sources- Primary: Redwood regional observability (ingress/egress token counts, per-route latency histograms from our EU private control-plane probes).
- Secondary: Customer-provided telemetry (optional) accepted as corroborating evidence — must include request IDs and timestamped traces.
- Tertiary: Third-party probes (we recommend two providers) for independent verification.

2) Sampling & aggregation- Latency percentiles are computed on per-minute histograms aggregated into service-level windows. We report p50/p90/p95/p99 over a 5-minute rolling window for dashboarding and into 60-minute windows for SLA evaluation. Sampling: server-side instrumentation samples 100% of control-plane transactions; data-plane inference calls are sampled deterministically (1:N) with a configurable stride.

3) Clock sync- Redwood requires NTP sync across probes and customer gateways with <500ms drift for evidence to be admissible. If drift >500ms, we fallback to sequence-number-based ordering for attribution and will document mapping rules.

4) Regional attribution- Requests are attributed to the region where the authoritative compute completed the final token generation. For multi-region deployments we provide per-region metering. Cross-region fallbacks (e.g., traffic routed to a warm standby region) are flagged and excluded from primary-region availability calculations unless configured otherwise.

5) Synthetic probes & acceptance tests- For private deployments we run four synthetic probe points across Novus's chosen EU locations. Acceptance: 14-day dry run with 95th percentile latency below agreed threshold (TBD) and no loss of greater than 0.1% for control-plane calls. Probe spec attached.

6) Service credits & evidence- Credits are calculated monthly using a weighted availability formula (per-region capacity-weighted uptime). Claims must include Redwood telemetry exports, probe traces, and customer logs with correlated request IDs. Credits processed within 30 days of validated claim.

I'll attach a draft checklist and the probe spec workbook; Karthik will add the legal/contract phrasing for credits.

Attachments: probe_specification.xlsx; redwood_eu_private_telemetry_sample.json

Marta / Grace,

Adding contractual language for credits and evidence chain. A few clarifications we should lock before the final checklist: 

- Availability definition: we propose "successful control-plane transaction completion" as the atomic event. This excludes queued requests that time out pre-ingress. Please confirm Novus is aligned.

- Measurement windowing: for monthly credits we suggest computing per-region availability in rolling 1-hour windows, then aggregating to a calendar month using time-weighted averages to handle partial-day cutovers. This avoids single-minute blips from inflating credit calculations.

- Credit tiers: we will propose a three-tiered credit matrix (0.5%, 2%, 5% of monthly invoice) tied to >99.9%, 99.5-99.9%, and <99.5% monthly availability respectively. Legal can adjust exact percentages.

- Evidence package: Redwood exports (CSV of per-minute histograms), probe traces (PCAP-lite/trace bundles), and customer request-id mapping table. We require the customer mapping table for any claim that references customer logs.

If Novus needs tighter windows or more granular percentiles (e.g., p99.9), we can include that as an addendum with expected cost/engineering tradeoffs.

On doc sequencing: Grace will push a checklist draft for audit sign-off by COB Aug 4.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

Thanks Grace and Karthik — this is helpful and addresses most of our questions. Two quick follow-ups for the checklist before our audit sign-off: 

1) Can you add an explicit example of a validated credit claim (dates, raw numbers, and how the formula arrived at the credit amount)? We need a worked example for our procurement evidence binder.

2) On clock drift: Novus's on-prem gateways currently report occasional bursts up to ~750ms drift overnight during backups. If Redwood can document the fallback mapping rules (sequence-number-based attribution) and provide a short remediation checklist we can accept the <500ms rule with the fallback behavior documented.

If you can add those two items and send the PDF by COB Aug 4 we'll proceed with internal approvals.

Regards,
